speaker: lecturer
text: Today we compare supervised and unsupervised learning with practical examples.

speaker: lecturer
text: Supervised learning uses labeled data, where each input has a known target output.

speaker: lecturer
text: A common supervised task is email spam classification using historical labeled emails.

speaker: lecturer
text: Unsupervised learning has no labels and focuses on structure, such as clustering customers by behavior.

speaker: lecturer
text: K-means is a classic clustering algorithm that partitions data into k groups.

speaker: lecturer
text: Model evaluation differs: supervised models use metrics like accuracy and F1, while clustering uses silhouette score.

speaker: lecturer
text: Feature scaling is important for distance-based methods because large-scale features dominate Euclidean distance.

speaker: lecturer
text: In practice, teams often start with simple baselines before trying larger neural models.

speaker: lecturer
text: A baseline gives you a reference point and prevents overestimating complicated models.

speaker: lecturer
text: We also discussed data leakage, where test information accidentally influences training.

speaker: lecturer
text: Leakage can produce unrealistically high results that fail in production.

speaker: lecturer
text: Always split train and test data before heavy preprocessing and feature selection.
